signature: removeOccurrenceOfElement(intArr: number[], ele: number, isSlicedArr: boolean) -> { k: int, resultArr: number[] }, where resultArr is intArr.slice(0, k) when isSlicedArr, and intArr itself (mutated in place) when not
notes: Each input is [intArr, ele]; `isSlicedArr` is a test-harness choice, not part of the case data, so run every case through both branches. `expected.k` is the count of elements not equal to `ele`. `expected.prefix` is the kept elements in their original relative order. How to compare it depends on the branch: with isSlicedArr=false, assert `resultArr.slice(0, k)` (the returned array still holds all the original values, and everything at index >= k is deliberately left untested — the problem allows any values there, so swap-based and overwrite-based solutions produce different tails and both are correct); with isSlicedArr=true, assert the returned `resultArr` whole, since it is already trimmed to k. Pass a fresh copy of the input array to each call: the function mutates its argument.

cases.name: run of the target in the middle

edgeCases.name: single element not equal to target
